question: why do the role-conditioned mixtures leave the three-code triple near-unique at either level?
method: exact counts and conditional entropies (bits) over the first three codes of each persisted SID; the fourth column is the export collision counter
reading: Every arm keeps the triple near-unique: the baseline has 20425 triples (1.204 items per triple), R03 23248 (1.058) and R04 22995 (1.069). The difference between arms is in the level-2 branching: distinct L2 prefixes 7374 (baseline), 9257 (R03), 8781 (R04) over roughly 250-256 level-1 codes, i.e. 29-36 distinct second codes per first code, and 2.66-3.33 items per L2 prefix. The level-3 refinement then splits each prefix again (H(L3|L1L2) 1.90-2.20 bits). Neither the level-1 nor the level-3 *mixture* moved that branching, which is consistent with both rounds: the freedom lives in the assignment/codebook itself, not in where the mixture is applied.
next_direction: R05 must constrain the branching inside a prefix rather than the metric of a level: the cost matrix needs a behaviour-conditioned reuse margin (a curvature-weighted hinge that discounts codes already used by the same graphlet role inside the same level-1 cell), with the Sinkhorn rule unchanged, so the role-to-code coupling acts on the assignment margin rather than on a distance mixture.
